title: Left rail reorg: hypotheses, wireframes, and prioritized backlog
content:
Context:

We keep hearing two related asks from customers and internal teams: 1) the left navigation is noisy and hard to scan for task-level flows, and 2) routing + deep links are inconsistent when users switch between Workspace/Dedicated/Private contexts. This doc consolidates our working hypotheses about a left-rail reorg, quick wireframe notes (text-first), and a prioritized backlog for grooming with engineering and design.

Guiding goals (product goals visible from backlog prioritization):
- Make common tasks discoverable in <= 3 clicks from top-level console entry.
- Preserve model-centric flows (model page as hub) while surfacing operational actions (deploy, monitor, audit).
- Provide stable URL surface so bookmarks, SDK links, and support tickets map directly to console pages.
- Keep the left rail density appropriate: compact primary entries, expandable secondary items.

High-level hypotheses (to validate with analytics + user interviews):
H1: Grouping by "task" (Build, Deploy, Observe, Manage) reduces time-to-task for new users vs grouping by product surface (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
H2: A persistent contextual selector (workspace dropdown + region badge) reduces routing errors when switching capacity types.
H3: Flattening second-level pages for common workflows (create model, open rollout, see traces) will lower click depth at the cost of a slightly taller rail.
H4: Users prefer visible routing breadcrumbs in the header when left-rail items are aggregated.

What success looks like (measurable):
- 15% reduction in average click-depth to complete "Create deployment" across new users (90-day window).
- 20% drop in support tickets referencing "can't find X page" after rollout.
- No more than 3 regressions in load/lightweight navigation latency (SLO 200ms median nav render).

Proposed left-rail structure (text wireframe):
Primary (top to bottom):
- Home (dashboard) — overview + quick actions
- Workspaces (workspace switcher + list)
- Build (models, model catalog, upload, evaluations)
- Deploy (deployments, rollouts, instance pools)
- Observe (runs/traces, logs, metrics, alerts)
- Optimize (batching suggestions, quantization profiles, cost explorer)
- Security & Compliance (audit logs, KMS, access control)
- Settings (billing, org settings, integrations)

Secondary (expandable under primary):
- Under Build: + New model -> import/upload, + Eval sets, + Model versions
- Under Deploy: + New deployment wizard, + Canary rollouts, + Capacity map
- Under Observe: + Live traces, + Trace search, + Regression alerts

Routing rules notes (desktop + deep links):
- Canonical routes: /workspaces/{id}/build/models/{modelId}, /workspaces/{id}/deployments/{deploymentId}, /workspaces/{id}/observe/traces/{traceId}
- When a user switches workspace: attempt to preserve entity context (if modelId exists in target workspace then route there else route to workspace root). Show a toast: "Entity not present in X; redirecting to Workspaces > Home"
- Query params used for ephemeral views only (e.g., modal=true). Persistent entity states (selected filters, time ranges) should be encoded in path segments where possible for shareability.
- Backwards compatibility: support legacy routes (/models/{id}) by redirecting to canonical route and leave a 302 in place for 6 months; add telemetry event legacyRouteRedirect.

Wireframe details (notes for design handoff):
- Compact rail variant: icons + 1-line labels, hover expands to full names. Use for screens <= 1280px.
- Dense rail variant: icons + labels visible, secondary groups collapsed into accordions. Use for >= 1280px where vertical space is available.
- Workspaces control sits above rail (sticky), with quick-create button and last-used list.
- Breadcrumbs + contextual title live in header; breadcrumbs double as quick filters for nested pages.

Accessibility & internationalization: 
- Ensure focus trap and keyboard nav between rail and content; accelerated actions (press D for Deploy) — not for GA but for power user testing.
- Labels must be localizable; keep label length in designs to 30 chars to avoid truncation in German.

Prioritized backlog (grooming-ready items; quick estimates in story points):
P0 (high priority — must be in first-phase IA rollouts):
- CON-1132: Implement workspace selector component (3) — blockers: auth token scoping review (INFR-1423).
- CON-1140: Left-rail skeleton + compact/dense variants (5) — includes CSS variable theming and responsive breakpoints.
- CON-1145: Canonical routing table and redirect middleware (5) — engineering to own telemetry for legacy redirects.

P1 (next wave):
- CON-1153: Deployments quick-create in rail (3) — modal vs route decision needed.
- CON-1160: Breadcrumb component + stateful deep-link preservation (4) — pair with product analytics to capture failures.
- CON-1167: Accessibility keyboard nav polish and tests (2).

P2 (future / nice-to-have):
- CON-1180: Personalizable rail (pin favorite pages) (5) — depends on user prefs infra.
- CON-1192: Experiment: Task-first IA vs Product-first IA A/B (8) — requires feature-flagging + analytics gating.

Acceptance criteria highlights (for the P0 tickets):
- Workspace selector: dropdown lists workspaces with <200ms load for first 10 workspaces; selecting workspace updates path and sends analytics event workspace.switch.
- Left-rail skeleton: no visual shift > 100ms after initial render; CSS fallbacks for browsers not supporting container queries.
- Routing middleware: visiting legacy URL redirects to canonical URL and a telemetry event with legacyRouteRedirect=true is emitted.

Telemetry & validation plan (post-ship):
- Create dashboard: click-depth per task, nav render latencies, legacyRouteRedirect counts, support ticket volume weekly.
- Run 6-week staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) gated by nav render SLO and support-ticket signals.

Open questions / risks (to discuss in grooming):
- How do we present org-level vs workspace-level settings without duplicating entries? Proposal: surface org-only items in a separate section under Settings with a small org badge.
- Region/Capacity context: should region be global header badge or embedded in workspace selector? Needs product/infra sync — potential coupling to private deployment workflows.
- Linking to ephemeral views (runs, traces) from external systems: should we accept token-based ephemeral deep links? Security has concerns; schedule meeting with sec/compliance.

Next steps (action items):
- This week: design quick comps for compact/dense variants (Diego + Priya).
- Next week: grooming session with SRE + infra to confirm canonical routes and redirect approach (Samir).
- Add analytics tracking plan as a separate Confluence page (owner: Emma).

Notes-to-self: keep the first rollout conservative — prioritize predictable redirects and workspace selector stability over personalization. Record user interviews (3 enterprise customers + 5 internal support reps) during the 10% rollout window.
